Sesame-Topped Barbari Bread

Served at: Yalda Night

Makes 2 large loavesPrep 30 minCook 25 min

Barbari bread is a traditional Persian flatbread known for its thick, chewy texture and distinctive ridges. It is commonly served during Yalda Night, the Iranian festival celebrating the winter solstice, symbolizing warmth and togetherness as families gather to enjoy special foods and poetry.

Ingredients

  • 4 cups (480 g) all-purpose flour
  • 1 1/2 teaspoons salt
  • 1 tablespoon sugar
  • 1 tablespoon active dry yeast
  • 1 1/2 cups (360 ml) warm water
  • 2 tablespoons vegetable oil
  • 1/4 cup (60 ml) lukewarm water (for glaze)
  • 1 tablespoon baking soda (for glaze)
  • 1/4 cup (35 g) white sesame seeds

Method

  1. In a large bowl, combine the flour, salt, and sugar.
  2. In a small bowl, dissolve the yeast in warm water and let it sit for 5-10 minutes until frothy.
  3. Add the yeast mixture and vegetable oil to the dry ingredients and mix until a dough forms.
  4. Knead the dough on a lightly floured surface for about 10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
  5. Place the dough in a lightly oiled bowl, cover with a damp cloth, and let it rise in a warm place for 1 to 1.5 hours, or until doubled in size.
  6. Divide the dough into two equal parts and shape each into an oval loaf about 12 inches long.
  7. Place the loaves on a parchment-lined baking sheet.
  8. Using your fingers or the back of a spoon, create several long, parallel ridges along the surface of each loaf.
  9. Preheat the oven to 450°F (230°C).
  10. Prepare the glaze by dissolving the baking soda in lukewarm water.
  11. Brush the glaze generously over the loaves, making sure it fills the ridges.
  12. Sprinkle the sesame seeds evenly over the top of each loaf.
  13. Bake the bread for 20-25 minutes, or until golden brown and cooked through.
  14. Allow the bread to cool slightly before serving.

Tips

  • For a softer crust, brush the bread with melted butter immediately after baking.
  • You can substitute nigella seeds or a mix of sesame and nigella seeds for a different flavor.
  • Serve warm with feta cheese, walnuts, and fresh herbs, traditional accompaniments for Yalda Night.
